## The Premise {#about .section-heading data-eyebrow="01 · where this starts"}

```{=html}
<div class="bio-block">
  <span class="bio-avatar"><img src="pics/headshot-420.jpg" alt="Lindsey E. Wylie" width="420" height="576" /></span>
  <div class="bio-body">
    <p>I am a researcher trained in law and psychology, and for more than
    twenty years I have studied how courts work and how they could work
    better for the people who come before them. That work has taken me from
    observing a mental health court in Brooklyn to linking statewide court
    records, and today, at the National Center for State Courts, I lead
    studies of pretrial court reminders and domestic violence court data and
    work on projects spanning young adults, treatment courts, competency, and
    guardianship. With Eve Brank, I wrote <em>Aging and the Criminal Legal
    System</em> (APA, 2025).</p>

    <div class="credential-badges">
      <span class="badge-item">Ph.D., Social Psychology · concentration in Research
      Design &amp; Data Analysis</span>
      <span class="badge-item">J.D. · concentration in Health Law</span>
    </div>

    <p>I built Data with a Plot to develop my skills in a place where I could
    publish directly to the web, and because I loved the name too much to let
    anyone else have it. It has become the place where I bring data to life
    in a way I could only imagine before: data stories that follow a finding
    from the numbers to the people behind them, teaching exercises that let
    you test your own judgment against the evidence, and planning tools that
    help colleagues choose an evaluation, a display, or a format for their
    own work.</p>

    <p>I build most of this with Claude Code, and I work with it the way I
    supervised research assistants and interns: with written instructions,
    clear direction, and my final edits. Like a strong graduate student,
    Claude Code does excellent work with sufficient preparation, but I hold
    the final judgments and products. The code behind every page is public,
    and so are the data wherever they can be shared, because I want my work
    to be shared, checked, and replicated.</p>

    <p><a class="bio-cta" href="selected-work/">See the plot so far: publications and CV →</a></p>
  </div>
</div>
```
